reverse_outline.summary: Chapter goals: decide placement, consistency, partitioning, retention and erasure of listing data
Business stake: buyers need true listings, regulators need proof of data handling
Architect stake: cheap copies multiply stale or unlawful data without registry, budgets and erasure paths
Three key points: one system of record, per-path consistency promises, retention and erasure per data class
Failure patterns addressed: search as system of record, ghost inventory, deal-shaped architecture
Event-driven copies raise three questions: which copy is right, how stale others may be, how deletion reaches all
Why the answers matter: price freshness, sold items in alerts, rebuilding search, provable erasure
Chapter scope and neighbouring chapters it relies on and feeds
Roadmap of the chapter and its legal evidence

results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

Every outline summary of a body unit matches the controlling idea of its aligned spec paragraph, in spec order (p01-p53, including in-practice after corrections); the five callout entries map to no spec paragraph.

Only Partitioning ¶2 was marked two_ideas (Tradeyard's shared cluster / Vinted's Vitess migration). The spec's p25 declares both as one idea: the cost of one store for all, with Vinted as a parallel case of the same capacity pressure; the paragraph keeps that single claim. The parallel-vs-counter-case confusion is recorded under flow_is_followable.
Every body unit supports one of S1-S5 as its section declares; introduction, judging sections and conclusion trace to the thesis.

Each table and figure is introduced and interpreted (seven copies -> four observations; kinds-of-copy table -> rebuildable-or-governed rule; retention table -> the two judgement rows; erasure outcomes -> nine-day response); quotations (Fowler, Vinted) and sources (GDPR, DSA, Ondernemersplein, Adevinta, Kleinanzeigen) are each tied to the point they support.

All declared transition_in relationships are expressed at their boundaries (e.g. 'The copies need names', 'The concepts now need stores', 'With the stores in place', 'Those obligations differ by data class', 'An erasure request tests both the registry and the retention schedule', 'Like erasures, corrections must reach every copy'). The weak antecedent at the start of Retention ¶4 is recorded under flow_is_followable.

Both readers describe the organising principle as the spec's prerequisite order (case, concepts, architecture with registry, placement, retention before erasure, corrections, then evidence and the standard judging sections); no section is 'unclear' to either reader. Material lost-thread points are listed as separate failures.

The retention schedule is shown before Femke's September case but dated after it, so the text has to repair the chronology twice (here and in Erasure ¶3); both readers stopped to work out which came first. The dating is mandated by p29's controlling idea and the spec's flow rationale, so removing the inversion requires a spec change.

The reader predicts the spec roadmap in order (bike in seven places, concepts, architecture, partitioning, retention, erasure, corrections, then Vinted/Adevinta practice, trade-offs, verticals, failure modes, Chief Architect's view, questions), the three questions and the thesis claims, and the evidence kinds (GDPR, DSA, Dutch rules, Vinted, Adevinta, fictional Veldmark). AC-2's expected text still places documented practice after architecture; the spec roadmap (current contract) places it after corrections, which is what the reader predicted. The reader noted the 'In this chapter' callout orders topics slightly differently (minor).

The reader gives the erasure case, scope resolution to identifiers, fan-out events, per-copy receipts matching the expected outcomes (SoR anonymized, 410 + CDN purge + removal request, media deleted, warehouse personal rows deleted, fraud case retained under Art. 17(3)(e) to a stated end, payments 7 years with restricted access, e-mail provider delete instruction), closure from the ledger and the registry removing the next search; and read-your-writes from the SoR or a version token. Buyer staleness budgets are not restated but are not needed for the seller complaint.

Replica, search index and cache rebuildable (freshness problem, purge on removal); archive, evidence store, warehouse (partly) and e-mail logs not, each with owner, purpose, retention and deletion path written down first, legal basis/access control, personal-data split and erasure job, processor contract with Art. 19 notification and delete instruction; 'rebuildable or governed' stated.

Country first (schema/database per country, country in every key, hash within large countries), global hash for one huge market or a cross-border catalog like Vinted, single writer per brand with read models near it, multi-writer only when latency or sovereignty demands it per Vinted's 2026 reasoning, replicas and backups inherit retention and erasure obligations.
